parsed.elsewhere_quote:
A positive integer is uniquely determined by its exponents $v_p(\cdot)$, and only primes dividing some initial $a_i$ contribute; hence
$$\boxed{\,M \;=\; \prod_{p\ \mathrm{prime}} p^{\,\gcd\big(v_p(a_1),\, v_p(a_2),\, \dots,\, v_p(a_N)\big)}\,}$$
parsed.explanation: The objection is correct: if an absent prime q is allowed in d, then every positive v_q(d) divides the zero valuations, so arbitrary q-powers can be adjoined and no maximal d exists. The boxed valuation formula and its choice-independence are nevertheless proved correctly elsewhere. Restricting d to primes dividing at least one initial entry repairs the remark.
